title: D1 serverless SQLite database basics
snippet: D1 is Cloudflare's serverless SQLite database. Each database has a UUID used in account scoped endpoints; name queries resolve the UUID first. Bind it to a Worker as a d1_databases binding to use env.DB.
summary: Create, identify and query a D1 database through REST or a Worker binding.
code:
wrangler d1 create my-db
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$ACCOUNT_ID/d1/database"

# wrangler.toml
[[d1_databases]]
binding = "DB"
database_name = "my-db"
database_id = "<uuid>"

title: Execute SQL over the D1 REST API
snippet: POST /accounts/{account_id}/d1/database/{database_id}/query with {sql, params, timeout} returns per-statement results, changes, rows_read and duration in meta. SELECT rows land in results.
summary: Run parameterized SQL statements and read changes/duration metadata.

title: D1 schema migrations with wrangler
snippet: Keep schema changes in migration files: D1 supports a maximum of 100 migration files and 5 consecutive pending migrations per session. Apply with --remote against production.
summary: Apply DDL migrations non-interactively and keep them versioned.
code:
mkdir -p migrations
cat > migrations/0001_init.sql <<'SQL'
CREATE TABLE users (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, email TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL);
SQL
wrangler d1 migrations apply my-db --remote
wrangler d1 migrations list my-db --remote

title: D1 query limits, batches and pitfalls
snippet: D1 rejects CREATE DATABASE and extension SQL like pragma/ATTACH; parameter binding cannot appear in the column list of an index, or in LEFT JOIN's right-hand ON clause; LIKE is case-insensitive (PRAGMA case_sensitive_like).
summary: Common D1 restrictions to check before sending SQL.

title: Cloudflare Workers deployment and environments
snippet: Workers deploy to production and optional preview environments. List scripts via GET /accounts/{id}/workers/scripts, deployments via /deployments, and routes via /workers/routes.
summary: Deploy a Worker, then inspect its environments and rollout history.
code:
npx wrangler deploy
npx wrangler versions upload
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$ACCOUNT_ID/workers/scripts"
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$ACCOUNT_ID/workers/scripts/my-worker/deployments"

title: wrangler.toml configuration reference
snippet: The Worker config declares main, compatibility_date, vars, bindings and routes. compatibility_date pins the runtime behaviour; changing it can alter Worker semantics.
summary: Minimal, valid wrangler configuration for a router Worker.
code:
name = "my-worker"
main = "src/index.ts"
compatibility_date = "2025-01-01"
workers_dev = true

[vars]
ENV = "production"

[[routes]]
pattern = "example.com/*"
zoned_name = "example.com"

[[kv_namespaces]]
binding = "CACHE"
id = "<namespace_id>"

title: Secrets and environment variables in Workers
snippet: Secrets are encrypted and environment scoped. Put them in .dev.vars (gitignored) and set them with wrangler secret put NAME; plain vars live in wrangler.toml [vars] or per environment.
summary: Store and roll API tokens as Worker secrets rather than in code.
code:
echo -n "$CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN" | npx wrangler secret put CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN
npx wrangler secret list
npx wrangler secret delete CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN

# local only
echo "CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN=dev_token" >> .dev.vars

title: Workers routes and zone routing
snippet: Account level routes (GET/POST /accounts/{id}/workers/routes) map a pattern to a script without touching zone config; zone scoped routes live on /zones/{zone_id}/workers/routes.
summary: Attach route patterns to a Worker and manage them via API.
code:
POST /accounts/{account_id}/workers/routes
{"pattern":"example.com/api/*","script":"my-worker"}

# equivalent wrangler.toml
[[routes]]
pattern = "example.com/api/*"
zoned_name = "example.com"

title: Worker bindings: KV, D1, R2, secrets, queues
snippet: Bindings inject typed clients onto env: KV (env.CACHE), D1 (env.DB), R2 (env.BUCKET), Durable Objects, queues, services and AI. Binding names must be unique per Worker.
summary: Declare storage and service bindings so Worker code receives env objects.

title: Cron triggers and scheduled handlers
snippet: Cron triggers run the scheduled handler on an UTC schedule via [triggers] crons. Supports regular cron expressions (5 field) plus seconds via the six-field form on paid plans.
summary: Run periodic maintenance work inside a Worker on a schedule.

title: Live Worker logs with wrangler tail
snippet: wrangler tail streams console.log, exceptions and fetch events for a deployed Worker in real time; --format json gives machine readable events, --filter restricts by level or header.
summary: Watch production Worker logs without a debug build.
code:
npx wrangler tail my-worker --format json --duration 30
npx wrangler tail my-worker --format json --filter "(event = fetch)"
npx wrangler tail my-worker --format json --filter "(log.level = error)"

title: Workers limits (CPU, memory, size)
snippet: Workers free plan: 10ms CPU per request, 128MB memory, ~1MB compressed script (10MB paid). Popularity limits are enforced on requests per minute at the edge.
summary: Check platform limits before profiling a slow or rejected deploy.
code:
# number of Workers routes may be limited by plan
wrangler whoami
wrangler deployments list --name my-worker

title: Workers KV namespaces and key-value ops
snippet: KV is a replicated key-value store: 1 KiB max key, 25 MiB max value, 512 KiB per metadata; writes are eventually consistent (up to 60s propagation).
summary: Create a namespace and read/write keys via API or binding.
code:
npx wrangler kv namespace create CACHE

# REST
curl -X PUT -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  --data-binary @value.txt \
  "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$ID/storage/kv/namespaces/$NS/values/my-key"

await env.CACHE.put('my-key', 'value', { expirationTtl: 60 });

title: KV REST endpoints: write key with TTL and metadata
snippet: PUT a value with query expiration_ttl (seconds, min 60) and metadata (JSON, max 1024 bytes). GET /values/{key} returns the body; GET /metadata/{key} returns attached metadata.
summary: Set keys with expiry and JSON metadata through the REST API.
code:
PUT /accounts/{account_id}/storage/kv/namespaces/{ns_id}/values/{key}?expiration_ttl=60&metadata=%7B%22v%22%3A1%7D
Content-Type: text/plain
Body: value

GET /accounts/{account_id}/storage/kv/namespaces/{ns_id}/metadata/{key}

title: KV quotas and request limits
snippet: KV limits: 1 key/value pair per request, key list max 1000 keys, 1000 write ops/sec per account, 1 write per key per second. Lists are lexicographic with cursor pagination.
summary: Where KV is and is not appropriate; batching strategy.
code: GET /accounts/{account_id}/storage/kv/namespaces/{ns_id}/keys?prefix=u_&limit=100&cursor=...

title: R2 object storage buckets
snippet: R2 is S3-compatible object storage with zero egress fees. Bucket operations live under /accounts/{id}/r2/buckets; object reads/writes go to the R2 data plane endpoint.
summary: Create buckets and operate on objects without S3 gateway costs.

title: R2 object listing and writes
snippet: POST /accounts/{id}/r2/buckets/{bucket}/objects/list with prefix, limit and cursor returns objects plus a truncated flag and cursor for the next page.
summary: Page through object keys in a bucket using prefix and cursor.

title: Presigned URLs for R2
snippet: R2 issues presigned S3 URLs through an S3 client with R2 credentials (Account ID, Access Key, Secret Key). Presign PUT for uploads, GET for private downloads.
summary: Hand a browser a time-limited upload/download URL without proxying bytes.

title: Zones and DNS records overview
snippet: A zone is a domain on Cloudflare, resolvable by GET /zones?name=example.com. DNS records live under /zones/{zone_id}/dns_records with type, name, content, ttl and proxied flags.
summary: Resolve a zone id, then list or mutate its DNS records.
code:
GET /zones?name=example.com
GET /zones/{zone_id}/dns_records?type=A&name=api.example.com
POST /zones/{zone_id}/dns_records
{"type":"A","name":"api.example.com","content":"203.0.113.10","ttl":1,"proxied":true}

title: DNS record types (A, AAAA, CNAME, TXT, MX, SRV, CAA)
snippet: A/AAAA map names to IPs, CNAME aliases another name (cannot coexist with other types at the same name), TXT holds verification strings, MX sets mail exchangers with priority, CAA restricts certificate issuers.
summary: Pick the right record type before upserting content.

title: Create or update a DNS record idempotently
snippet: Fetch by type+name first: PATCH /zones/{zone_id}/dns_records/{record_id} when found, otherwise POST to the collection. ttl 1 means automatic; proxied is only valid for A, AAAA and CNAME.
summary: Safe create-or-update flow by natural key (type + name).

title: Proxy status (orange cloud), TTL and caching
snippet: proxied=true routes traffic through Cloudflare (CDN, WAF) and hides origin IPs; ttl=1 is automatic (120s default minimum with proxy on). TXT/MX and other types are DNS-only.
summary: Decide whether a record should be proxied and which TTL to set.
code: {"type":"A","name":"origin.example.com","content":"203.0.113.10","ttl":1,"proxied":false}

title: Cloudflare API tokens and scopes
snippet: Create scoped API tokens (DNS:Edit, Account:Read...) instead of Global API Keys. Verify with GET /user/tokens/verify; send Authorization: Bearer on every request. Tokens are account secrets - never log them.
summary: Least-privilege token setup and verification for this server.
code:
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/user/tokens/verify"
# suggested grants for cloudflare-mcp:
#   Account: D1, Workers KV, Workers Scripts, R2 - Read/Edit
#   Zone: DNS:Read/Edit, Zone:Read

title: v4 API response envelope and errors
snippet: Every v4 response is {success, errors[], messages[], result, result_info}. Pagination uses page/per_page/result_info.has_more. Retry 429 with Retry-After, honour rate limits per token.
summary: Parse Cloudflare responses and paginate list endpoints correctly.

title: Workers observability, alarms and queries
snippet: Workers Logpush, Workers Observability and wrangler tail cover invocations, errors and CPU time. console.log is retained when observability enabled; tail gives immediate streaming.
summary: Instrument and inspect Worker behaviour in production.
code:
observability = { enabled = true, head_sampling_rate = 1.0 }

# wrangler.toml
[observability]
enabled = true

title: Durable Objects: state, coordination, sqlSession
snippet: Durable Objects give a single-threaded instance with transactional storage (in-memory cache + SQLite persistence). Migrations declare the class with new_sqlite_classes for SQLite-backed storage.
summary: Use a Durable Object when you need strongly consistent coordination.

title: Local development with wrangler dev
snippet: wrangler dev runs a local Miniflare instance (default local bindings) on port 8787; --remote targets real resources. Use --dry-run to validate config without deploying.
summary: Validate Workers and bindings before touching production.
code:
npx wrangler dev --port 8787
npx wrangler dev --remote
npx wrangler deploy --dry-run
npx wrangler whoami

title: Tool-driven infrastructure automation patterns
snippet: Prefer typed tool calls with idempotent semantics (upsert by natural key) over shelling out to a CLI: responses are structured JSON, credentials stay server-side, and errors map to stable types (configuration, api, wrangler).
summary: Guidance for composing multi-step Cloudflare changes safely.
code:
1. cf_system_status           -> verify auth + capabilities
2. cf_d1_list_databases       -> resolve name to id
3. cf_d1_query(..., params)   -> run parameterized SQL
4. cf_d1_query('PRAGMA table_info(users)') -> inspect schema
5. cf_dns_upsert(..., comment) -> idempotent record change

title: Diagnosing common Cloudflare API failures
snippet: 6003 invalid API token (scope or rotation), 10000 authentication error, 9109/81057 unknown zone or record, 7003 routing/unknown path, 429 rate limited. Check /user/tokens/verify first and CLOUDFLARE_ZONE_MAP for zone ids.
summary: Map Cloudflare error codes to the correct fix.

title: Queues and Streams for async work
snippet: Queues decouple Workers with producers and consumers (batch size/max timeouts), Hibernatable WebSockets and DLQs. R2-backed video uses Cloudflare Stream with direct upload + play codes.
summary: Choose Queues for at-least-once async processing, Stream for video.

title: WAF, rate limiting and Access policies
snippet: Zone level WAF custom rules, rate limiting rules and Bot Fight Mode protect origins behind proxied DNS. Cloudflare Access adds identity-aware zero-trust access in front of applications.
summary: Layer edge security after DNS records are proxied.

title: Caching: Cache API, cache rules and purge
snippet: caches.default in a Worker caches at the edge by URL; Cache Rules shape CDN cache behaviour; purge via POST /zones/{zone_id}/purge_cache with purge_everything or tags/hosts/url lists.
summary: Control edge caching from Worker code or zone configuration.

title: Configuration migration gut-check
snippet: When changing Cloudflare configuration through an MCP tool: capture the previous record/resource state first, prefer idempotent upserts, keep DNS TTLs low during cutovers, and verify with a read tool before declaring done.
summary: Operational checklist before mutating production resources.
code:
cf_dns_list zone=example.com name=app.example.com type=A   # before
# change (ttl=1, proxied=false during cutover)
cf_dns_upsert zone=example.com name=app.example.com type=A ...  # apply
# verify
# re-read: expect action=updated and previous content captured for rollback

title: Session and connection limits at the edge
snippet: Cloudflare terminates TLS and reuse happens per PoP: clients should use connection pooling (http keep-alive) rather than one-shot requests. Node httpx pools per unique origin by default.
summary: Client-side performance guidance for API-heavy tooling.
code:
import httpx
client = httpx.Client(base_url=API, headers={'Authorization': f'Bearer {token}'})  # keep-alive
